DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.1233.setting: University Hospital Galway, Emergency Department and ward consults (Liaison Psychiatry/on-call Psychiatry)

cycle1.result: 28 presentations; 23 (82.1%) seen in ED; 19 (67.9%) needed an interpreter; 16 (57.1%) related to low mood with or without suicidal ideation; 16 (57.1%) referred to a Community Mental Health Team.

DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.1233.other_findings: Descriptive service review with no standard; suggests translated patient information documents to improve care.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.430.topic: Low FODMAP diet response in IBS

cycle1.result: Of 80 treated, 46 had follow-up data; at least 70% improved for each symptom; bloating 93% improved, flatulence 92% improved; mean stool consistency 5.21 to 4.16 (Bristol); mean stool frequency 3.87 to 1.56 per day.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.430.other_findings: 27 of 80 did not attend follow-up and 7 were awaiting follow-up; use of the diet increased each year since 2009.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.536.standard: NICE NG225: comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment for self-harm or suicidal ideation, using standardised template headings

cycle1.result: Presenting Situation 100%; Mental State Examination 98%; Risk Summary 98%; Psychiatric Formulation 92%; Social Situation 81%; Physical Health History 75%; Safeguarding Concerns 71%; Carer/Parent's Understanding 40%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.536.other_findings: Psychiatric headings well completed but social aspects, especially family understanding, poorly assessed; qualitative work on barriers planned.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.039.topic: DNAR and ceilings of care documentation
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.039.setting: Sligo University Hospital, Model 3 hospital, adult medical inpatients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.039.standard: Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) national DNAR guidelines

cycle1.result: DNAR status documented in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion 45%; reasons if patient discussion excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if relatives excluded 18%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.039.intervention: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.

cycle2.result: DNAR status 35% and reasoning 32% (unchanged); patient discussion 61%; reasons if excluded 66%; relatives' discussion 48% (unchanged); reasons if relatives excluded 25%; ceilings of care documentation increased (ICU three-fold, intubation two-fold) but still under 15%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.039.other_findings: Ceilings of care documentation remained under 15%; authors propose a Ceilings of Care document.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.038.setting: Specialist Geriatric Ward, Connolly Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.038.standard: Irish National Audit of Dementia-2 (INAD-2) recommendations and National Clinical Guideline 21 dementia care standards

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 69%; delirium recognition 53%; nutritional care 84%; food within reach 38%; safe mobility 80%; pain assessment 0%; personal preferences documented 40%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.038.intervention: Multidisciplinary Dementia/Delirium Care Bundle: staff training, bedside identifiers, personalised care plans and environmental changes (orientation boards, activity resources, dementia signage).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 87%; delirium recognition 89%; nutritional care 95%; food within reach 100%; safe mobility 100%; pain assessment 100%; personal preferences 88%; antipsychotic prescribing practices improved by 37%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.038.other_findings: 27 patients across pre- and post-implementation audits; documentation gaps remain and sustainability work is needed.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.148.setting: Nottingham University Hospitals, high-volume oesophago-gastric resection unit
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.148.standard: Trust ERAS protocol for oesophagectomy and gastrectomy (oral intake, drain, catheter and epidural removal, mobilisation, discharge medications)

cycle1.result: Oral diet started on time 85%; epidural removal 52.6% (95% within 24 h); catheter 55% (90%); apical drain 55.6% (100%); basal drain 53.8% (85.7%); abdominal drain 81.8% (90.9%); daily mobilisation 65%; VTE prophylaxis 100%; discharge medications 86.7% to 100%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.148.other_findings: All mobilised within four days; mean stay 9 days post-oesophagectomy; 3.2% emergency department return rate.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.033.setting: Geriatric wards, Royal Glamorgan Hospital, district general hospital, South Wales

cycle1.result: Baseline cognition, falls history, memory loss and personality changes each documented in fewer than 40% of patients.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.033.intervention: Concise collateral history proforma introduced (PDSA 1), then refined after staff feedback (PDSA 2).

cycle2.result: After second PDSA cycle: falls documented in all patients; memory loss, mood and personality changes each over 75%; smoking, alcohol and finances consistently captured.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.033.other_findings: First PDSA re-audit (30 patients, 2 months) showed falls and baseline cognition over 70% and mood, memory and personality coverage more than doubled.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.294.topic: Missing person rapid risk assessment completion
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.294.setting: Royal Cornhill Hospital, NHS Grampian, general adult, older adult and learning disability wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.294.standard: Missing Person Protocol Rapid Risk Assessment proforma completion, in line with the National Framework for Missing Persons

cycle1.result: Previous audit figures not given; first audit in 2017.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.294.intervention: Teaching around the RRA and weekly review of the RRA at MDT meetings.

cycle2.result: 100% of notes contained the RRA proforma; average completion of all sections 87.5%; 14.5% improvement compared with previous audit and 21% since 2017.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.294.other_findings: Brief Admission Details poorly completed and no ward had completed the Return to Ward Questionnaire; completion best in learning disabilities and worst in general adult wards.

cycle1.result: Appropriate albumin use by indication 30%; about 800 vials per month.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002534.intervention: Dissemination of evidence-based recommendations, new electronic order set, education, prescriber interviews and a return policy change to reduce wastage.

cycle2.result: Appropriate use 50% (p<0.0001); usage fell to 450 vials per month, mainly less 5% albumin (p<0.0001); less wastage (p=0.017).

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002534.other_findings: Mortality, length of stay and new kidney replacement starts unchanged; estimated annual saving CAN $300 000.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11653.topic: Antipsychotic high-dose and PRN prescribing governance
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11653.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Leicester
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11653.standard: BNF dose limits, PRN governance (instructions, review, benzodiazepine PRN 4 weeks or less) and HDAT form completion

cycle1.result: Exceeding BNF maxima 1%; polypharmacy 5.6%; PRN not reviewed 1.9%; PRN instruction missing 1.1%; benzodiazepine PRN over 4 weeks 0.26%; HDAT forms completed 1/378 (0.002%).

cycle2.result: Exceeding BNF maxima 2.9%; polypharmacy 10.4%; PRN not reviewed 1.45%; PRN instruction missing 2.1%; benzodiazepine PRN over 4 weeks 2.70%; HDAT forms 3/482 (0.62%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11653.other_findings: Most measures worsened; recommends EHR hard-stops, automated benzodiazepine review prompts, a polypharmacy proforma and HDAT training, with a third cycle.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.293.setting: Galway University Hospital, tertiary acute stroke centre
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.293.standard: Practice compared with the intervention arms of the RESTART and SO-START trials (no guideline stated)

cycle1.result: 42 (75%) survived to discharge; 25% of those on antiplatelets restarted at one year (mean 20 weeks to restart); 70% of those on oral anticoagulation restarted at one year (mean 14 weeks); none with MRI-confirmed amyloid angiopathy (n=5) restarted (p<0.01).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.293.other_findings: Fewer patients restarted antiplatelets than anticoagulants despite trial evidence supporting both.

DOI:10.1111/anae.14734.setting: 28 centres, cardiology and cardiac surgical patients under anaesthesia, ACTACC national audit

cycle1.result: 17 major complications (palatal injury or gastro-oesophageal disruption), incidence 0.08% (95% CI 0.05-0.13%), about 1:1300; 7 deaths, 0.03% (95% CI 0.01-0.07%), about 1:3000.

DOI:10.1111/anae.14734.other_findings: About 40% of patients with a complication died; most complications occurred in patients without known risk factors.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.86.setting: Teiripe sa Bhaile integrated early supported discharge programme, St James's Hospital and The Meath Community Unit, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.86.standard: Chartered Society of Physiotherapy hip fracture rehabilitation: start within 72 hours of discharge and two hours of rehabilitation per week until goals met, with an outcome measure

cycle1.result: All patients seen within 72 hours of referral and received on average 3 hours per week of rehabilitation; mean FIM improvement 36.35; mean hospital LOS 14.8 days with TsaB versus 54 days.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.86.other_findings: Rockwood frailty score improved from 5.6 to 3.14; no 30-day readmissions; about 4 bed days saved per week.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11687.topic: Antipsychotic side-effect monitoring (GASS) for depot patients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11687.setting: Swale Community Mental Health Team, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11687.standard: Trust and NICE guidance: GASS at one month after starting depot and at least every six months thereafter

cycle1.dates: 1 Nov 2023 to 30 Jan 2024 (monitoring reviewed Jan 2022 to Oct 2023)
cycle1.result: 5% (1/20) had six-monthly GASS assessments.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11687.intervention: Staffing improvements including a new pharmacy team and increased awareness of guidelines.

cycle2.dates: 15 Jan 2025 to 30 March 2025 (monitoring reviewed Jan 2024 to Dec 2024)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11687.other_findings: Reasons for missed assessments were often undocumented; patient refusals persisted.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16267.topic: Peri-operative cardiac arrest in frail older patients
DOI:10.1111/anae.16267.setting: Royal College of Anaesthetists 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) activity survey and cardiac arrest registry

cycle1.result: 1676 (26%) of 6466 patients over 65 were frail (CFS 5 or more); 156 (18%) of 881 cardiac arrests were in frail over-65s, incidence 1 in 1204 and mortality 1 in 2020, about 2.6-fold higher than non-frail.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16267.other_findings: Hip fracture, emergency laparotomy, emergency vascular and urological surgery were the commonest procedures in frail patients who arrested.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002632.topic: Blood test result actioning and communication
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002632.setting: 57 general practices across all four UK nations (Primary care Academic CollaboraTive)

cycle1.result: Auditors agreed with actioning in 89.9% (n=2311); specified action carried out in 89.7% (1015/1132); no evidence of result communication in 47% (n=1210), and in 30.6% (360/1176) with abnormal results.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002632.other_findings: Of 117 unactioned results, 2 were high risk and 1 came to harm; large variation between practices; practices received benchmarked reports.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.235.setting: Medical gerontology rehabilitation ward, Tallaght University Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.235.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard

cycle1.result: 26 (83.9%) wore incontinence wear, 21 (80.8%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 13 (41.9%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.235.intervention: Continence added to NCHD teaching schedule and MDT proforma adjusted to include a patient-specific continence record.

cycle2.result: 27 (67.5%) wore incontinence wear, 19 (70%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 18 (45.7%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.235.other_findings: Prevalence of incontinence unchanged; many patients preferred incontinence wear, so future work should engage patients.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.005.topic: Fracture liaison service falls assessment and exercise referral
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.005.setting: Irish Fracture Liaison Services, national FLS Database and Facilities Audit
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.005.standard: IOF Capture the Fracture KPIs: falls risk assessment and strength and balance exercise referral

cycle1.result: 51% of 3,770 fragility fractures assessed for falls risk (range 2-90%); one third of these referred or advised to self-refer to strength and balance programmes; at 16 weeks 56% contactable, of whom 21% had started a programme.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.005.other_findings: Five of six Dublin hospitals reported access to programmes versus none outside Dublin; four hospitals reported no patient exercise participation at 16 weeks.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.291.setting: Luton & Dunstable University Hospital, general surgery
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.291.standard: NICE guidance: liver function tests and ultrasound first line for suspected gallstones, MRCP/EUS if not detected

cycle1.result: 44 CT scans; CTAP as first scan in 38 patients.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.291.intervention: Findings presented at local general surgery clinical governance meeting and communicated to hospital doctors.

cycle2.result: 31 CT scans (30% decrease); CTAP as first scan in 21 patients (45% drop).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.291.other_findings: Ultrasound still not always first line owing to clinical judgement, different requesting specialties, unawareness of NICE guidance and ultrasound delays.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.429.setting: Four Black Country Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Teams (Dudley, Walsall, Sandwell, Wolverhampton)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.429.standard: All patients discharged from CRHT should receive planned follow-up within 3 months of discharge

cycle1.result: Wolverhampton: all had 72-hour follow-up but 12% lost to long-term follow-up or in crisis first; Dudley 51% and Sandwell 47% followed up within 3 months; Walsall followed up all unless discharged to GP.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.429.other_findings: 30 patients went into crisis before planned follow-up; one patient died by suicide 4 months after discharge without follow-up.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.12.setting: Southmead Hospital, North Bristol NHS Trust, emergency laparotomy patients aged 70 and over
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.12.standard: NELA standard: geriatrician review of all patients aged 70 or over, target 80%

cycle1.result: Geriatrician review 16% (n=5); inpatient mortality 23% (n=7); discharge home 68% (n=21); mean LOS 17.6 days.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.12.intervention: Dedicated gastrointestinal surgery geriatric liaison service established in August 2018 replacing ad hoc reviews.

cycle2.result: Geriatrician review 86% (n=43); inpatient mortality 14% (n=7); discharge home 76% (n=38); mean LOS 17.9 days.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.12.other_findings: National compliance with this standard was 23%; one patient in each cohort newly discharged to a nursing home.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.017.topic: Bone protection first dose before discharge in orthogeriatric patients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.017.setting: Ageing and Complex Medicine orthogeriatric service, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.017.standard: NHFD and NOGG: bone health plan and first dose of bone protection during hospital stay

cycle1.result: 90% had a bone health plan; only 33% of these received first dose before discharge; treatment delayed in 56% and not given in 10%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.017.intervention: Teaching session, new trust guidelines, redesigned electronic note for documentation and inclusion in orthogeriatric induction.

cycle2.result: 100% had a bone health plan; 81.25% given first dose of IV bisphosphonate before discharge (48.25% improvement).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.017.other_findings: Barriers included unclear documentation, inadequate vitamin D/calcium replacement and not obtaining consent during admission.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljae090.273.setting: Paediatric dermatology clinics, Birmingham Children's Hospital
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljae090.273.standard: Dedicated consultant clinic slot directly bookable by ED (local booking rules)

cycle1.result: Only 85 (41.1%) of slots used by ED referrals; 92 (44.4%) GP, 15 (7.2%) internal, 9 (4.3%) external, 6 (2.9%) own department; median wait 2 weeks; attendance 84.7%.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljae090.273.other_findings: ED treatment appropriate in 56% and not assessable in 28%; problem resolved by appointment in 20%; plans to reinforce booking rules and reinstate dermatology teaching in ED.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.517.setting: Specialist NHS drug service, West London
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.517.standard: Best practice recommendations for initiation and monitoring of naltrexone

cycle1.result: All patients had keyworker involvement and physical health checks; 18 of 28 took naltrexone over one week; 16 reported reduced cravings; 6 abstinent and 10 partial response; 9 of 18 had side effects.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.517.other_findings: Diagnostic coding and recording of the offer of written information need improvement.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.064.setting: Ipswich Hospital, UK district general hospital
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.064.standard: Comparison with the PANC study; Royal College of Radiologists guidance on CT use

cycle1.result: Gallstones 45% (PANC 50.6%), idiopathic 33% (PANC 22.4%), alcohol 18%; 45% of idiopathic cases had further screen and 10% EUS; CT used in 51% (PANC 53%); antibiotics within 48 hours in 55% (PANC 34.6%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.064.other_findings: 33% of patients with diagnostic amylase had a CT, suggesting CT overuse against RCR guidance.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.096.setting: Geriatric service, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin, tertiary hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.096.standard: HIQA National Standard for Patient Discharge Summary Information (25 variables), 80% completeness per variable

cycle1.result: 17 of 25 variables 100% complete (automatically included); discharge medication and follow-up over 80%; allergy status 27%; blood and radiological investigations 49%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.096.other_findings: Automated fields achieved 100%; recommends automatic inclusion of investigation reports.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.551.topic: Lifestyle factor documentation in psychosis clinic letters
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.551.setting: Leicestershire Early Intervention in Psychosis team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.551.standard: Gold standard: all seven pillars of lifestyle medicine explored at each medical review

cycle1.result: For all domains 'not mentioned' was most common, ranging from 48.6% to 70.8%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.551.intervention: Findings shared with team, educational poster created and electronic system being adapted to record lifestyle factors (re-audit planned in 12 months).
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.551.other_findings: Second commonest finding was 'mentioned with no further details' for all domains except refraining from toxins.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10641.standard: NICE, IDF and WHO: metabolic screening every 6 months for patients on long-term psychotropics

cycle1.result: 15.15% had complete screening within six months; 30.30% incomplete; 54.55% missing data.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10641.intervention: Structured metabolic screening tool, GP coordination and staff education.

cycle2.result: 66.67% screened within six months; 33.33% not screened within six months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11399.topic: Mental Health Act T3 medication authorisation compliance
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11399.setting: 16-bed Old Age Psychiatry ward, Hollins Park Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11399.standard: Mental Health Act medication authorisation (T3) forms: zero administrations outside authorised route or frequency

cycle1.result: Four off-T3 medication incidents; mean staff knowledge score 58%; confidence 3.7/5.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11399.intervention: Visual whiteboard above the drug trolley identifying patients with active T3 forms, plus targeted teaching using real incidents.

cycle2.result: Zero off-T3 incidents for four consecutive months; knowledge score 71%; confidence 4.3/5.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11399.other_findings: Staff reported the visual prompt aided adherence.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.3.046.setting: Southland Hospital, Invercargill, orthopaedic and geriatric shared care

cycle1.result: Orthopaedic ward LOS 9.8 days; rehabilitation ward LOS 19.9 days; patients with a complication 71.6%.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.3.046.intervention: Collaborative orthopaedic and geriatric shared care model introduced in 2012.

cycle2.result: Orthopaedic ward LOS 7.5 days (p=0.138); rehabilitation ward LOS 9 days (p<0.001); patients with a complication 57% (p=0.045).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.3.046.other_findings: Adjusted odds of complication reduced by 12% (p<0.001); no difference in mortality.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10699.setting: Ely Neighbourhood Team, Old Age Community Mental Health Team, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10699.standard: NICE guidance on routine antipsychotic monitoring (BMI, ECG, bloods, lipids, HbA1c, pulse and BP, LFT, EPSE) over 12 months

cycle1.result: All offered monitoring (1 declined); blood monitoring 94%; pulse and BP 100%; 29% (5) lacked an ECG despite needing one; 65% (11) not asked about EPSE/movement disorders.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10699.other_findings: Recommends closer collaboration with GPs to improve ECG and movement disorder monitoring.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10565.topic: CAMHS to adult mental health transition
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10565.setting: North Devon Liaison and Home Treatment Teams, Devon Partnership NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10565.standard: Devon Partnership NHS Trust transfer of care SOP (8 core transition standards), target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 100% of specialist CAMHS users secured AMHS input; 57% had a care plan with defined exit; 14% given explanation why services could not be offered; 14% allocated a doctor on transfer; 29% had a documented joint CAMHS-AMHS meeting.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10565.other_findings: Of 51 young people, 28 were formerly known to CAMHS and 12 underwent transfer; re-audit planned after change.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.135.setting: 18 UK district general hospitals, children with suspected appendicitis (PAPAYA study)

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 21%; PAS not correlated with histological appendicitis (rho=0.004, p=0.951); ultrasound findings not associated (p=0.336); 87% with non-visualised or equivocal ultrasound had appendicectomy with normal histology.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.135.other_findings: Retrospective cohort study showing wide variation in diagnostic pathways.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.134.setting: Medical gerontology ward, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.134.standard: HIQA National Standard for Patient Discharge Summary Information

cycle1.result: 97% (30/31) had discharge summaries; patient identifiers, dates, clinical course, investigations, medications and author 100%; referral source 20%; dietary interventions 13%; immunisation 0%; follow-up guidance 77%; social care actions 27%; advice and future plans 20%; information given to patient/carer 10%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.134.other_findings: Ward doctors now receiving education on documenting functional status, social care and diet; mandatory electronic fields suggested.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.203.setting: University Hospital Waterford trauma unit and pilot six-bed rehabilitation unit at Kilcreene Regional Orthopaedic Hospital

cycle1.result: Median wait for off-site rehabilitation across the south-east was six days.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.203.intervention: Pilot six-bed hip fracture rehabilitation unit with orthogeriatric-led weekly MDT meetings and ward rounds.

cycle2.result: 15 of 17 transferred same day or day after being rehabilitation ready; longest wait three days (two patients).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.203.other_findings: Hospital average hip fracture LOS 17 days (19 days awaiting off-site rehab) versus national average 12 days.

PMID:17387351.setting: Pain clinic, Sunnybrook Health Science Centre, tertiary teaching hospital, Toronto

cycle1.result: 174 completed follow-up; 55 (31.6%) had no benefit; 119 (68.4%) had good (>50%) to excellent (>80%) pain relief lasting 6 to 24 months.

PMID:17387351.other_findings: 35 patients lost to follow-up or had incomplete data.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.468.setting: South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust, trust-wide
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.468.standard: NICE guidance on EUPD: no drug treatment specifically for EUPD, time-limited crisis prescribing only, regular reviews and written information

cycle1.result: 81.6% (71) prescribed medication; 39.4% (28) consistent with time-limited prescribing; 57.7% (41) had timely reviews; 4.2% (3) had evidence of written information.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.468.other_findings: Results presented to the Clinical Reference Group and a working group formed to improve prescribing and written information.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.592.setting: Adult inpatients of a general psychiatric hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.592.standard: NICE: prolactin checked 6 months after starting then every 12 months, with enquiry about symptoms (not required for aripiprazole, clozapine, quetiapine, olanzapine under 20 mg)

cycle1.result: Prolactin measured in 80.6% (25/31) in last year; 48% (12/25) hyperprolactinaemic, with action in 5 (41.7%); of 9 on drugs needing monitoring for a year, 8 (88.9%) measured, 5 elevated, action in 3 (60%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.592.other_findings: Hyperprolactinaemia in 58.3% of women and 38.5% of men; 25.8% on two antipsychotics.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae277.023.setting: Orthogeriatric care, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae277.023.standard: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit 2023 and 2024 recommendations: timely vitamin D and IV zoledronic acid

cycle1.result: Vitamin D administration 14.71%; IV zoledronic acid 12.12%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae277.023.intervention: Staff education, process standardisation, Bone Health stickers and whiteboards, formal referral pathways and decision-making protocols.

cycle2.result: Vitamin D administration 100%; IV zoledronic acid 95.45%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae277.023.other_findings: 165 records analysed November 2023 to May 2024; initial data capture inaccurate owing to inconsistent referral system use.

DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.10431.setting: General adult community mental health service, HSE North Dublin Mental Health Services
DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.10431.standard: NICE: 6-monthly TFTs and U&Es, documented lithium levels, clinical review of results and structured follow-up

cycle1.result: Fell short across all standards, with deviations of 21% to 36%.

DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.10431.intervention: Nurse-led lithium monitoring clinic (January 2025) with structured appointments, reminders, GP collaboration and systematic documentation, plus team psychoeducation.

cycle2.result: All parameters over 85% compliance; largest gain in documentation and clinical sign-off of investigations (+29.2%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.225.setting: Mossley Hill older adult inpatient and outpatient service, Liverpool
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.225.standard: NICE NG97 and BNF/SPC renal function (eGFR) recommendations, with GP communication

cycle1.result: Renal function documented in 68%; GP informed of medication change in 86%; initiation mostly in line with NICE.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.225.other_findings: Recommends an electronic memantine prescribing checklist.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.283.topic: Antipsychotic use for non-cognitive symptoms of dementia
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.283.setting: Acute care older adult ward, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Median 14 patients per month on an antipsychotic (range 7-18); median 5 on PRN antipsychotics (3-12); median 2 given IM injection (1-3).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.283.intervention: Multicomponent PDSA intervention: antipsychotic decision algorithm, CNS-led review, behaviour charts, staff education and coaching, 'Get-to-Know-Me' document and distraction resources.
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.283.other_findings: Some evidence of reduced PRN and IM use in new admissions, but long-stay patients had high antipsychotic use; reasons for PRN often undocumented.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.506.setting: UK tertiary referral centre (Southmead Hospital, Bristol)
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.506.standard: Melanoma Focus standards for ano-uro-genital mucosal melanoma

cycle1.result: 83% first assessed in gynaecology urgent suspected cancer clinic; 83% biopsied before resection; staging CT 93%; lateral margins involved in 53%; no patient had formal quality-of-life assessment.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.506.other_findings: 28% had died; local standard operating procedure developed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.614.setting: CAMHS, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, trust-wide
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.614.standard: NICE guidelines on prescribing for children with autism spectrum disorder

cycle1.result: 44% had alternative interventions before medication; consent documented in 62%; psychotropics started at minimum effective dose; follow-up within 3-4 weeks in 70%; 77% on sleep medication, 55.5% of whom had alternatives first.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.039.topic: Pre-operative fluid fasting in hip fracture
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.039.setting: Tertiary university hospital, Cork University Hospital, operative hip fracture patients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.039.standard: Fasting 6 hours for solids and 2 hours for clear fluids; SipTilSend clear fluids until transfer to theatre

cycle1.result: Previous PDSA cycle average fluid fasting 3 h 45 min.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.039.intervention: Reinforcement through staff education, ward prompts and MDT engagement with nursing, orthogeriatric and anaesthetic teams.

cycle2.result: Mean fluid fasting 11.2 hours (median 9.75 hours, range 0-36 hours), worse than previous cycle.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.039.other_findings: No peri-operative aspiration events; compliance with SipTilSend deteriorated over time.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8793569.topic: COVID-19 impact on foot and ankle surgery
EPMC:PMC:PMC8793569.setting: 43 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland (FAlCoN national audit)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 infection 0.53% (n=35), highest in lockdown 2.11% and lowest after 0.16%; lockdown activity 24.44% of pre-lockdown; elective activity 1.73% in lockdown and 10.72% after.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8793569.other_findings: Highest regional infection rate in South East England (3.21%); national peak 1.37% in final week of lockdown.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.134.setting: General medical and surgical wards, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin, patients over 65
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.134.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard

cycle1.dates: Three-day period at start of continence awareness month
cycle1.result: All had documented continence status; of 44 continent pre-admission, 12 had incontinence wear as inpatients.

cycle2.result: All had documented continence status; of 40 continent pre-admission, 14 had incontinence wear as inpatients.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.134.other_findings: Rationale for incontinence wear varied and was sometimes undocumented; use increased between audits.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.216.setting: Psychiatry of Old Age service, Sligo Leitrim Mental Health Service
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.216.standard: Developing national Model of Care for Dementia in Ireland and best practice

cycle1.result: Lack of standardised memory assessment, delays in neuroimaging and laboratory results, and gaps in staff training (no figures reported).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.216.intervention: Care pathway document, staff training with standardised assessment scales, improved laboratory/radiology booking and an OT cognitive remediation group.
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.216.other_findings: Preliminary data show improved satisfaction in the cognitive remediation group; equipment audit led to improvements.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.028.topic: Adjuvant chemotherapy outcomes in pancreatic cancer
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.028.setting: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

cycle1.result: 209 (69%) had adjuvant chemotherapy; median OS gemcitabine 21.6 months (ESPAC 4 25.5), gemcitabine-capecitabine 25.2 months (ESPAC 4 28), FOLFIRINOX 19.9 months (PRODIGE 24 54.4).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.96.setting: Bournville Ward, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, geriatrics
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.96.standard: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham guidelines: conservative measures (fluid, fibre, exercise) before laxatives

cycle1.result: Constipation recognised in 57%; 64% of these developed it in hospital; 20% had complications.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.96.intervention: Teaching sessions for ward staff and weekly MDT discussion of constipated patients, with early non-laxative measures if bowels not opened for over 2 days.

cycle2.result: Patient education up 19%, cause recognition up 27%, non-laxative methods up 30%; inpatient-developed constipation down 6% and complications down 4%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.96.other_findings: Only a small impact on constipation prevalence and complications.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.214.topic: Psychotropic prescribing audit tool in residential care

cycle1.result: Pilot of audit tool acceptability: all 15 auditors found the audit relevant and training and manual useful; some needed extra support.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.214.other_findings: Difficulties included reading handwriting, locating information and prescribing inconsistencies; suggestions to shorten manual and add glossary.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.005.setting: Acute Frailty Unit and two Elderly Care wards, Maidstone General Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.005.standard: European Society of Cardiology heart failure guidelines 2023

cycle1.result: Phenotype in clerking 18% (5/28) and discharge notes 39% (11); iron deficiency investigated 43%; iron infusion 5/12 (42%); SGLT2i 10/22 (45%); ACE/ARB/ARNI 3/9 (33%); MRA 3/9 (33%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.005.intervention: Departmental teaching, discussing HF phenotype at board rounds, ward round teaching, governance presentation and posters.

cycle2.result: Phenotype in clerking 23/42 (54.7%) and discharge notes 27/42 (64.3%); iron deficiency investigated 69%; iron infusion 14/15 (93%); SGLT2i 22/28 (79%); ACE/ARB/ARNI 17/18 (94%); MRA 13/13 (100%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.288.setting: Heddfan Psychiatric Unit, Wrexham, general adult inpatients, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.288.standard: Core psychiatry trainee competencies, NICE guidelines, local BCUHB physical health policy and Department of Health VTE guidance

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed incomplete vital data at clerking (figures not reported).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.288.intervention: New admission clerking proforma developed using fishbone and driver diagrams and PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Repeat audits over one year showed improved completion of medication, allergy, legal and forensic status, MSE, risk, VTE assessment and investigations (figures not reported).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.288.other_findings: Barriers included no ECG machine and investigations done but not documented.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.063.setting: NELA Leads at hospitals across England and Wales (national survey)

cycle1.result: 166/289 leads (57.4%) and 117/167 hospitals (70.1%) responded; pre-operative nutritional screening 39.2% and assessment 45.8%; albumin still used for malnutrition risk 73.5%; post-operative pathways 71.7%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.063.other_findings: 71.2% said nutrition risk is an important missing NELA data item; barriers were time, training, organisational support and ownership.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.211.setting: National Office of Clinical Audit Orthogeriatric Network multidisciplinary workshop

cycle1.result: Strong consensus on including nutritional assessment and monitoring in CGA; barriers included limited dietetic support, portion sizes, modified diets and repeated fasting.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.211.other_findings: Facilitators included dietetic access, protected meal times, red trays, protein supplements and 'sip til send'; national guidance in development.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10608.topic: Antidepressant prescribing in children and adolescents
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10608.setting: Tonteg Hospital, Taf Ely area, Rhondda Cynon Taf, child and adolescent services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10608.standard: NICE guidelines for depression in children and young people: psychological therapy before antidepressants

cycle1.result: Psychological therapy before antidepressants 63% (29/46); single antidepressant 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10608.intervention: Recommendation that psychotherapy be considered before starting antidepressants and that this be included in GP letters.

cycle2.result: Psychological therapy before antidepressants 82% (9/11); single antidepressant 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10608.other_findings: Comorbid diagnoses 82.6% (38/46) initially and 54.5% (6/11) at re-audit; only fluoxetine and sertraline used.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.13.009.topic: VTE after foot and ankle surgery

cycle1.result: 99 symptomatic VTE within 90 days (0.87%); 3 VTE-related deaths (0.03%).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.13.009.other_findings: Independent predictors were Achilles rupture (OR 11.62 operative, 14.41 non-operative) and ASA III/IV (OR 3.64).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.241.setting: Inpatient psychiatric units in North Wales (Heddfan, Ablett, Hergest), Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.241.standard: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services (2014) and PRSB Mental Health Discharge guidelines (2018)

cycle1.result: Allergy status not mentioned in 96% at Hergest; same-day GP receipt 13% Ablett, 0% Hergest, 100% Heddfan; risk history 0% Hergest and Heddfan, 12% Ablett; crisis contacts 0% across sites.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.241.other_findings: In 49% of Ablett summaries medication was the only field completed; care coordinator details 0% at Heddfan and Ablett.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.916.topic: Contacting the on-call doctor via switchboard
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.916.setting: Abraham Cowley Unit, four-ward inpatient psychiatric unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.916.standard: Trust protocol: duty doctor contacted via switchboard, target 80% of calls

cycle1.result: 25% (5/20) of calls via switchboard.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.916.intervention: Posters above ward telephones and assessment suite telephone, and direct handover of policy to nurses in charge.

cycle2.result: 88% (7/8) of calls via switchboard; 80% standard met.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.214.setting: Four early intervention service hubs, Birmingham
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.214.standard: POMH-UK quality improvement programme standards for valproate prescribing

cycle1.result: Target symptoms documented in all; 94% started as inpatients; 55% on off-licence preparation, 93% of these without documented rationale and 93% without discussion with patient; adequate community monitoring 74%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.214.other_findings: Semi-sodium and sodium valproate used interchangeably despite not being bioequivalent; limited side-effect screening documented.
